entity: Hackathon brainstorming session - Claude skill for improving descriptions
generating_prompt: Describe the people and vibe in 100 words.

claims.text: Applications span translation, advertising, and social modeling
claims.note: Rarest domain trio - most distinctive claim in the description

claims.text: Third person grounds ideas in user behavior, writing, and taste
claims.note: Specific role fingerprint; writing and taste is an unusual pairing

claims.text: One speaker pushes structure and theory, trying to formalize the concept
claims.note: Distinct theorizer archetype; useful for session classification

claims.text: Overlapping, playful, slightly distracted by logistics
claims.note: Good imagery for display but low retrieval value
Subjective claim; nearly everyone claims this

claims.text: Excitement from sensing a genuinely expandable idea
Visibly energized by each other's momentum
Earliest stage of invention - language unfinished, room messy
claims.note: Stage label useful for classification; otherwise common
~60% of hackathon sessions - near-zero retrieval info

within_scope.change: Replace chaotic but generative with a specific observed behavior
within_scope.reason: Matches ~60% of sessions. Replace with something only this session does, e.g. one person keeps circling back to a single metaphor while the others build on it.

within_scope.change: Replace ambitious builders with a specific interaction dynamic
within_scope.reason: Near-universal at hackathons. Describe how they specifically interact, e.g. the theorizer and app-generator frequently interrupt each other.

within_scope.change: Cut the final sentence; use word count on one concrete observation
within_scope.reason: Excitement from sensing a genuinely expandable idea is the lowest-information sentence. Replace with a specific phrase or moment from the transcript.

prompt_level.change: Add: Name the concept or idea being explored
prompt_level.reason: Naming the concept narrows from 10,000 to ~10 transcripts instantly. Change prompt to include: ...and the concept being discussed.

prompt_level.change: Add: Note whether the group converged or diverged by the end
prompt_level.reason: Convergence/divergence is a high-value classification signal. Only ~30% of sessions converge - this contributes ~1.7 bits.

prompt_level.change: Add: Identify the team or project name if mentioned
prompt_level.reason: Team metadata dramatically narrows retrieval. If multiple sessions are from the same hackathon, team name is the key discriminator.
